forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.previous_proof_nl:
Let n := a + b + r, and for m >= 0 write (q)_m := product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j). Then
P_{a,b,r}(q) = ((q)_{r+b}/(q)_{r+a}) / ((q)_b/(q)_a) = (q)_{r+b}(q)_a / ((q)_{r+a}(q)_b).
Using the standard formula for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients,
[N choose K]_q = (q)_N / ((q)_K (q)_{N-K}),
we obtain
[n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q = (q)_a (q)_{n-a} / ((q)_b (q)_{n-b}).
Since n - a = r + b and n - b = r + a, this is exactly
(q)_{r+b}(q)_a / ((q)_{r+a}(q)_b) = P_{a,b,r}(q).
So P_{a,b,r}(q) is a quotient of two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients with the same top n.

Now we prove that this quotient is a polynomial. Fix a positive integer d, and let e_d be the exponent of the cyclotomic polynomial Phi_d(q) in P_{a,b,r}(q). In the product (q)_m = product_{j=1}^m (1 - q^j), the factor Phi_d(q) appears once for each j divisible by d; hence its exponent in (q)_m is floor(m/d). Therefore

e_d = floor((r+b)/d) + floor(a/d) - floor((r+a)/d) - floor(b/d)
    = (floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d)) - (floor(b/d) - floor(a/d)).

By the hypothesis, this number is >= 0 for every positive integer d. Also e_d = 0 for d > r+b, so only finitely many e_d are nonzero. Hence
P_{a,b,r}(q) = product_{d >= 1} Phi_d(q)^{e_d}
belongs to Z[q].

Finally, 0 <= a <= b <= n, and we have shown that
P_{a,b,r}(q) = [n choose b]_q / [n choose a]_q
is a polynomial in q. Applying the allowed dependency root_semantic_sketch with k = b and l = a, we conclude that every coefficient of this polynomial is nonnegative. Therefore P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and all of its coefficients are at least 0.
payload.role_in_assembly: This is the main positivity theorem for the reduced shifted interval product; once established, the parent theorem follows immediately from the reductions.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If integers a, b, r satisfy 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, and if for every positive integer d the floor inequality floor((r + b) / d) - floor((r + a) / d) >= floor(b / d) - floor(a / d) holds, then the finite product from i = a + 1 to b of (1 - q to the power r + i) divided by (1 - q to the power i) is a polynomial with integer coefficients, and every coefficient is at least 0.

Define P of a, b, r at q by the finite product over i from a + 1 to b, with empty product equal to 1 when a = b
For all positive integers d, the floor inequality holds: floor((r + b) / d) - floor((r + a) / d) >= floor(b / d) - floor(a / d)
Then P of a, b, r at q is a polynomial in the integer polynomial ring and all of its coefficients are nonnegative

payload.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

result_payload.proof_summary: I can verify the algebraic rewrite P_{a,b,r}(q) = (q)_{r+b}(q)_a / ((q)_{r+a}(q)_b) = [a+b+r choose b]_q / [a+b+r choose a]_q, with the empty-product case a=b giving P_{a,a,r}=1. I can also prove polynomiality directly from the floor hypothesis by cyclotomic exponents: for each d>0 the exponent of Phi_d(q) in P_{a,b,r}(q) is floor((r+b)/d)+floor(a/d)-floor((r+a)/d)-floor(b/d), which is nonnegative by the assumption, so P_{a,b,r}(q) lies in Z[q]. What I could not complete is the required independent argument that all coefficients of this polynomial are nonnegative, without appealing to the forbidden root theorem/root semantic sketch or to a heavy external theorem not present in the allowed context.

result_payload.stuck_point: After proving polynomiality, I could not find a fully self-contained construction showing coefficientwise nonnegativity for the general quotient product. Several natural ideas (pairing numerator and denominator exponents into q-integers, reducing to smaller intervals, or using semigroup/monomial-basis interpretations) break down on examples such as (a,b,r)=(1,3,3), where the product is positive but does not admit the simplest divisibility pairing. So I cannot honestly supply the final positivity step within the permitted dependency constraints.
